## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-fascicle Suí-period Chinese translation of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* by Dharmagupta 笈多. Signature: 「隋大業年中三藏笈多譯」 ("translated by the Tri-piṭaka Master Jíduō during the *Dàyè* era") — *Dàyè* 大業 = 605–618 CE under Suí Yángdì. The opening *praṇāma*-formula 「歸命一切佛菩薩海等」 ("homage to the ocean of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas") is distinctive. The title 能斷 ("able-to-cut") is a calque-translation of *vajra-cchedikā* preserving the Sanskrit semantic structure more closely than the earlier 金剛 ("Vajra") used in [T235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023).

**Abstract**

T238 is the fifth of the six Chinese *Vajracchedikā* translations ([T220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001)(9), [T235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023), [T236](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0024), [T237](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0026), [T238](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0027), [T239](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0028)) and is dated to the *Dàyè* era (605–618 CE) at Cháng'ān. Dharmagupta's translation idiom is more literal and Sanskrit-preserving than [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) Kumārajīva's; the title's *néngduàn* lexicon foreshadows [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) Xuánzàng's later choice of vocabulary in [K016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0029) and [T239](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0028) ([義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) Yìjìng's). For the *Vajracchedikā* tradition broadly, see [T235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023).
